title: Daily Brief Source Catalog
description: Catalog of news, government, venue, and community sources used by the Daily Brief collector. The document contains a single top-level `sources` array.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Complete list of monitored sources. Each entry describes one outlet, venue, park, museum, or institution.

name.title: Name
name.description: Human-readable unique name of the source.

locality_index.title: Locality Index
locality_index.description: Geographic tier of the source. Legend: 0 = Canton Township; 1 = Surrounding cities (Plymouth, Livonia, Westland, Wayne, Belleville, Northville); 2 = Ypsilanti & Ann Arbor; 3 = Detroit & Metro Detroit; 4 = Statewide Michigan.

location.title: Location
location.description: Free-text geographic description of the source's coverage or physical location, e.g. "Canton, MI" or "Detroit & Metro Region, MI".

category.title: Category
category.description: Fine-grained editorial/operational category for the source (e.g. "Township / Government", "Live Music Venue", "Regional Local News").

type.title: Type
type.description: Broad classification of the source (e.g. "Official Government", "Venue", "Student Journalism", "Public Broadcast").

frequency.title: Frequency
frequency.description: How often the source is expected to be polled or is known to publish. "4hours" denotes four-times-daily polling.

url.title: URL
url.description: Primary website URL for the source. Must be an absolute http(s) URL.

events_url.title: Events URL
events_url.description: Direct calendar/events URL when one exists; null when the source has no dedicated events page.

description.title: Description
description.description: Short summary of what the source covers and why it is monitored.

engine.title: Collection Engine
engine.description: Collection strategy. 'auto' (default) fetches feeds and crawls over plain HTTP (with curl_cffi TLS impersonation) first, escalating to a headless browser only when the result looks blocked or JS-shell-like, and to a commercial scraping API only as a last resort. 'http' forces the plain-HTTP crawler. 'browser' forces the headless-browser crawler. 'api' fetches seeds through the configured scraping API. All engines produce the same content.md/meta.json output.

crawl_urls.title: Crawl URLs
crawl_urls.description: Additional seed URLs crawled in addition to `url` and `events_url`. Useful for server-rendered event/listing routes that the landing page does not link directly (e.g. a Drupal views feed).

feed_urls.title: Feed URLs
feed_urls.description: RSS/Atom/ICS/JSON-feed URLs fetched over plain HTTP and converted to text. May also be a public Instagram profile URL (recent post captions, which often carry event dates and ticket links, are extracted). Best-effort structured, dated content that bypasses page rendering.

max_pages.title: Max Pages
max_pages.description: Optional per-source override of the global --max-pages page budget (useful for bounding pathologically slow or paywalled sources).

enrich_strategy.title: Best Enrich Strategy
enrich_strategy.description: Hint for the best event-enrichment strategy for this source. 'auto' (default) learns per source: the first strategy that fills missing fields is cached under processed/enrich_strategies.json and tried first thereafter (JSON-LD Event markup, an ical feed, the URL-embedded date, or the touch-up model), with the full chain as fallback so page-shape changes self-heal. Set 'jsonld', 'ical', 'llm', or 'url_date' to try that strategy first; 'none' disables detail fetches for sources whose pages are dead ends (forms, third-party landing pages).
